newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank sets unchanged repo operation.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank sets unchanged repo operation.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday left its key interest rate, the repo rate, at 4.10 percent in a new operation.
The reverse repurchase operation, the first since December 17 when the Riksbank lowered the repo rate by 25 basis points, returned to a weekly routine after the holiday period.
The operations will run from January 8 to January 15.

All primary dealers are invited to submit bids to the Riksbank by 0900 GMT on January 7 with the lowest accepted volume 200 million crowns and highest accepted volume 40 billion crowns, the central bank said.
A Reuters poll of 10 analysts found the market did not expect the Riksbank to cut the repo rate in its first operation for 1997.
But economists were expecting further cuts in the repo rate that has been lowered from 8.91 percent from the start of 1996.
The repo is the central rate in the bank's interest rate corridor with its other key rates, the deposit and lending rates, currently standing at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.
